instruction: When and where does CSS360 meet?
response: Class meets Tuesday and Thursday from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. in UW1 room 302.

instruction: Is there a required textbook for this course?
response: No. There is no required textbook. Course materials come from a range of sources that should be free through Canvas or the UW Library Proxy.

instruction: What is the main project in CSS360?
response: You will work in a group to build, analyze, and deploy a Discord bot across multiple sprint tasks. Teams may propose alternative bot ideas, but the default project is a Discord bot.
sourceSection: Project: Developing a Discord Bot as a Team

instruction: What is the best way to ask a general course question?
response: Start with a public message on Discord so classmates can see the answer. Private Discord works for individual questions, and Canvas is required for grade-related discussion.

instruction: Where should I discuss a grade I received on an assignment?
response: All grade-related discussion must happen through Canvas, not Discord or email. Book a private calendar timeslot within one week of the grade being released if you want a grade consultation.

instruction: Can I discuss my grade publicly in Discord?
response: No. Grade-related discussion must take place through Canvas. Use Discord for general course questions, not for conversations about grades or assessment feedback.

instruction: The instructor has not replied to my message. What should I do?
response: If you have not received a response within 48 hours, send a polite follow-up via Discord direct message. A delayed reply is usually unintentional due to high message volume.

instruction: What should I do if I know I will miss class?
response: Submit the course absence form at least one hour before class begins. Advance notice avoids a no-call, no-show penalty, but it does not create a makeup opportunity for missed in-class work.
sourceSection: Course absence form and Your Presence in Class

instruction: Does submitting the absence form let me make up the missed activity?
response: No. Filing the absence form avoids a no-call, no-show penalty, but there is no direct way to make up missed in-class activities. You may be called upon more often in later classes to balance participation.

instruction: What happens if I miss class without filing the absence form?
response: Not filing the form counts as a no-call, no-show and will impact your in-class activities grade. Always submit the absence form if you must miss, arrive late, or leave early.

instruction: If I miss several classes, can I still earn full credit for in-class activities?
response: Missing too many classes can eventually make it impossible to receive full credit for in-class activities, because participation cannot be balanced indefinitely through cold calling alone.

instruction: Am I responsible for material I miss when absent?
response: Yes. After an absence, you are responsible for obtaining class notes, handouts, assignments, and any other information you missed.

instruction: What should I complete before coming to class?
response: Finish all assigned readings and watch all recorded lectures before the associated class session. You are fully responsible for this preparation because lectures are not generally delivered during class meetings.

instruction: Does the instructor lecture during class meetings?
response: No. The course uses a flipped format, so the instructor does not generally deliver lectures during synchronous class meetings. Class time is used for standups, case discussions, questions, and project work.

instruction: How much time should I plan to spend on this course each week?
response: Plan for about 10 hours of weekly coursework plus 4 hours in class and up to 1 hour in lab or office hours. If you are spending substantially more or less, consider booking an office hours appointment to discuss strategies.

instruction: Can I read assigned material more than six days ahead of the due date?
response: The syllabus does not guarantee readings beyond six days ahead. If you plan to read more than six days in advance, contact the instructor first because details may still change.

instruction: What time are assignments due?
response: Unless otherwise noted, assignments are due at 11:59 p.m. Pacific time on the listed due date.

instruction: What types of assignments does this course include?
response: The course includes one group Discord bot project, one reflection essay, and possibly short low-stakes quizzes. There are no exams.

instruction: What file format should I use when submitting assignments on Canvas?
response: The syllabus does not specify file formats for every assignment. Check the assignment instructions on Canvas for each task's submission requirements.
sourceSection: Assignments and Websites and Technology Expectations

instruction: Can I use AI tools on the reflection essay?
response: No. AI tools are explicitly forbidden for the reflection assignment. The essay should use your own evidence from the bot project and real, viewable citations.
sourceSection: Reflection on Software Engineering and the Bot Project

instruction: How is the Discord bot project structured?
response: The project is broken into multiple tasks that build on each other, from environment setup through version 2.1. Teams use GitHub, Kanban boards, sprint planning, standups, pull requests, and tagged releases.
sourceSection: Project: Developing a Discord Bot as a Team

instruction: Can my team propose a different bot project idea?
response: Yes, but propose your idea early so there is time to iterate. Your idea may differ from what the course structure supports, so early discussion helps ensure timely completion.

instruction: What deliverables are required for the live bot demo?
response: During your 10-minute in-class slot, show your bot with the full group participating. Grades reflect preparation and participation; have your pre-recorded demo ready as a fallback if the live demo fails.

instruction: Can I use AI to write feedback for another group's bot?
response: No. The bot feedback assignment requires your own view grounded in your observations. Do not use AI tools for that assignment.

instruction: What happens if my group's bot project falls behind schedule?
response: The syllabus does not specify a single recovery plan for every delay. Check Canvas for current task deadlines, coordinate with your group in standups and Discord, and ask the instructor through Discord if you need course-specific guidance.

instruction: What three questions do you answer in standup?
response: In standup you report what you did since the last standup, what you will do before the next standup, and whether you have any blockers.

instruction: What do I need to do to receive standup credit?
response: You must be present during the synchronous standup, actively participate, and document your standup work on Discord.

instruction: Can I make up a missed standup by posting an update on Discord?
response: No. Sharing an update on Discord may be helpful, but it is not a substitute for synchronous standup participation. There is no direct makeup for a missed standup.

instruction: Will the instructor summarize case material during class?
response: No. The instructor will not summarize case material in class or cover it in lecture. You are expected to have read the case and class discussion starts from that preparation.

instruction: How can I prepare for cold calling in case discussions?
response: Use the Reading Note questions, which are finalized at least six days in advance. Writing out answers ahead of time is recommended, and you may brainstorm with classmates.

instruction: Are Reading Note answers collected for a grade?
response: No. Although preparing written answers is a good idea, Reading Note responses are not collected. Case discussion participation is assessed through in-class discussion instead.

instruction: How is the course grade broken down?
response: In-class activities are 50%, Sprint 1 is 10%, Sprint 2 is 15%, Sprint 3 is 15%, presentation work is 5%, and the reflection is 5%.

instruction: What percentage do I need for a 2.0 in this course?
response: You need at least 74.6% overall to receive a 2.0 for the course.

instruction: How is my individual contribution within a sprint graded?
response: The syllabus points to detailed sprint rubrics on the assessment page rather than a single formula in the syllabus. Check Canvas and the project rubrics for how your sprint work is evaluated.
sourceSection: Grading and SW Engineering Project Rubric

instruction: How do I challenge a grade I disagree with?
response: Book a private calendar timeslot within one week of the grade being released. During the consultation, be prepared to show specifically how your work meets the rubric and learning goals.

instruction: What overall percentage maps to a 4.0?
response: For this quarter, 97.0% maps to a 4.0 and 60.0% maps to a 0.7, with even spacing between those points.

instruction: Can I use my one 48-hour extension on any assignment?
response: No. Among Bot Project Tasks 1 through 6, you may use one 48-hour extension for exactly one task per quarter. Demo, feedback, and reflection assignments do not allow extensions.

instruction: What is the late penalty for project tasks?
response: Late completion generally causes a 20% penalty per 48-hour period after the deadline.

instruction: How do I request the one allowed 48-hour extension?
response: Use Canvas to make your request so it is private and trackable. The syllabus suggests saving the extension unless you truly cannot avoid using it.

instruction: Can the final reflection be submitted late with the normal 20% penalty?
response: No. No extension is possible for the reflection assignment because it sits at the end of the quarter and grades must be submitted on time.

instruction: Can I use AI on every assignment in this course?
response: No. AI use depends on assignment-specific instructions. Some assignments allow AI with citation, while others such as the reflection and bot feedback explicitly forbid it.

instruction: Am I responsible for verifying AI-generated information?
response: Yes. AI results can be biased or inaccurate, and you are responsible for ensuring that information you use from AI tools is accurate.

instruction: Is using AI for grammar and spellchecking allowed?
response: Yes. Grammar and spellchecking with AI is allowed even when other AI uses are restricted for an assignment.

instruction: Which websites and tools do I need for this course?
response: You need reliable access to Canvas, Discord, GitHub, Google Docs, Panopto, and the UW Library Proxy. Off-campus access to restricted materials may require the proxy or UW VPN.

instruction: Where are recorded lectures hosted?
response: Recorded lectures are hosted on Panopto. You are expected to watch lecture material before the associated class session.

instruction: When is the next open lab session?
response: Open lab dates are not listed as fixed times in the syllabus. Watch weekly Canvas announcements and Discord for upcoming open lab periods.

instruction: How far in advance should I book office hours?
response: Book at least 24 hours in advance. If you book less than 24 hours ahead, confirm the booking with a message on Discord because the instructor may miss it otherwise.

instruction: Is open lab the same as a private office-hours appointment?
response: No. Open lab is an optional drop-in period for questions and co-working. For focused one-on-one attention, book an office hours appointment instead.
sourceSection: Class format and structure and Office Hours

instruction: Are there exams in CSS360?
response: No. There are no exams. You may encounter short, low-stakes quizzes, but there is no final exam.

instruction: Are there no assessments because there are no exams?
response: No. Even without exams, the course still assesses you through in-class activities, three sprints, presentation work, the reflection, and possible low-stakes quizzes.

instruction: What should I do when the syllabus does not answer my question?
response: Check Canvas announcements and assignment instructions first. If you still need help, ask through the appropriate channel—usually public Discord for general questions or Canvas for grade-related issues.
sourceSection: Note about this Syllabus and Contact

instruction: Can I assume the syllabus will never change during the quarter?
response: No. The syllabus is a dynamic document. Core expectations are fixed, but readings, projects, and assignment details may shift. Monitor Canvas announcements and the syllabus wiki for updates.

instruction: Where do I find the Discord invitation for this course?
response: The Discord invitation link is in the Class Setup Checklist on Canvas. Check Canvas if you need joining instructions.

instruction: How much does each quiz count toward my final grade?
response: The syllabus mentions short low-stakes quizzes but does not specify individual quiz weights. Check Canvas for how any quiz is weighted if one is assigned.

instruction: Which bot project task should I use my 48-hour extension on?
response: The syllabus does not tell you which task to pick. You may use one extension among Tasks 1 through 6, so choose based on your needs and remember you cannot use it on demo, feedback, or reflection work.
